correctness.rationale: The finite-output obstruction is valid: if a multivalued problem reduces to a single-valued discrete problem with \(s\) outputs, at most \(s\) outputs can be persistently uniquely forceable. Continuity lets one successively extend the input prefix while keeping the same canonical oracle output name, contradicting a forced change of answer after \(s+1\) commitments. For \(\mathsf{cShuffle}_m\), every nonempty color set \(C\) is persistently uniquely forceable by extending any finite coloring so exactly the colors in \(C\) occur densely in every rational interval and all outside colors stop. Thus there are \(2^m-1\) forceable outputs, whereas \((\mathsf{LPO}^{\prime})^n\) has \(2^n\) outputs, ruling out all \(n<m\). The strict two-color sandwich combines this lower bound with the published upper and reverse-separation bounds.

originality.rationale: The Pauly–Pradic–Soldà full paper explicitly leaves the relation between \((\mathsf{LPO}^{\prime})^n\) and fixed-color \(\mathsf{cShuffle}_m\) as Open Question 30 after proving the global finite-parallel equivalence. Targeted Resultary search found no earlier fixed-color lower bound of one jumped-LPO bit per color. The general finite-output continuity lemma is not claimed as the novelty; the solved parameter lower bound is.

value.rationale: This closes the lower side of an explicit fixed-parameter Weihrauch question and decides the first open case exactly up to the known strict upper bound. The argument isolates a reusable discrete-output obstruction tied to the \(2^m-1\) persistent palettes.
